answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, an identity is verified by repeated modular squaring, where each result depends on the previous one; GPUs may run separate chains in parallel but cannot shortcut one chain’s sequential delay. Thus, a Sybil attacker can create clones, yet must pay the physical time and compute cost for each proof rather than obtain instant identities. A vertex may mark a chain’s start, while plume and tide label challenge inputs that prevent reuse of old work.
